title: Watermarks, late data, and deciding what to do with it

videos.script: Sales from nine o'clock to five past nine. When is that count finished? {{window}} At five past nine, by the clock on the wall? Not if a till is slow. At two in the afternoon, when Natal's till comes back? Then every answer waits five hours. {{wait}} A stream never tells you that it is finished with a minute. So a processor has to decide. {{decide}} It looks at the latest sale it has seen. It subtracts a margin. And it says: nothing older than this is coming. That line is a watermark. {{watermark}} When the watermark passes the end of a window, the window is emitted. A sale that turns up behind it is late. {{late}} Late sales can update a result, go to a topic of their own, or be dropped. Each choice has a price, and in this lesson you pay each one. {{choices}} You also measure the margin from real data. And you watch one empty partition stop every result in the stream. {{idle}}
